name: scp
description: Protects against destructive SCP operations like overwrites to system paths.

destructive_patterns.name: scp-destination-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: scp/pscp has a runtime-dependent or malformed destination that cannot be verified before execution.
destructive_patterns.explanation: A shell variable, expression, malformed URI, or otherwise unverified final operand can \ resolve to a protected local path or an arbitrary remote host. Use a literal destination \ so the engine can determine direction and target before the transfer runs.

destructive_patterns.name: scp-relative-traversal
destructive_patterns.description: scp/pscp uses parent-directory traversal in a remote relative destination.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Remote relative paths and tilde paths are resolved by the remote account. A `..` component \ can escape the account's apparent home/staging directory and overwrite a protected system \ location. Resolve the remote absolute path first and use a traversal-free destination.

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-windows-system
destructive_patterns.description: scp/pscp targets a protected Windows system directory on the remote host.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Copying into a remote drive root, Windows, Program Files, ProgramData, Boot, or EFI tree can \ overwrite operating-system files and make the destination host unusable. Stage the payload \ in a non-system directory and install it through a reviewed deployment mechanism.

destructive_patterns.name: scp-recursive-root
destructive_patterns.description: scp -r to root (/) is extremely dangerous.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Recursive copy to the root filesystem can overwrite critical system files, \ potentially rendering the system unbootable. This affects all system directories \ including /etc, /bin, /lib, and /boot.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Specify a target subdirectory instead of / \ - Use rsync with --dry-run to preview changes \ - Copy to /tmp first and move files individually

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-etc
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /etc/ can overwrite system configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /etc directory contains critical system configuration files including passwd, \ shadow, fstab, and network settings. Overwriting these can lock you out of the \ system or cause services to fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Copy to a staging directory first \ - Back up existing files before overwriting \ - Use configuration management tools (Ansible, etc.)

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-var
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /var/ can overwrite system data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /var directory contains variable data including logs, databases, mail spools, \ and application state. Overwriting this data can cause data loss and service \ disruptions.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use /var/tmp for temporary staging \ - Stop affected services before modifying their data \ - Back up existing data first

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-boot
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /boot/ can corrupt boot configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /boot directory contains the kernel, initramfs, and bootloader configuration. \ Corrupting these files will prevent the system from booting, requiring rescue \ media to recover.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use package manager for kernel updates \ - Keep backup kernels available \ - Test changes in a VM first

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-usr
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /usr/ can overwrite system binaries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /usr directory contains system binaries, libraries, and shared resources. \ Overwriting files here can break system utilities and installed applications.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use /usr/local for custom installations \ - Use package managers for system updates \ - Install to user directories when possible

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-bin
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /bin/ or /sbin/ can overwrite system binaries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /bin and /sbin directories contain essential system binaries required for \ basic operation. Overwriting these can make the system unusable and require \ rescue mode recovery.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Install custom scripts to /usr/local/bin \ - Use package managers for system updates \ - Test binaries in user directories first

destructive_patterns.name: scp-to-lib
destructive_patterns.description: scp to /lib/ can overwrite system libraries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The /lib and /lib64 directories contain shared libraries required by system \ binaries. Overwriting these can cause immediate system instability and prevent \ commands from running.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use package managers for library updates \ - Install custom libraries to /usr/local/lib \ - Use LD_LIBRARY_PATH for testing
